_readme: Each entry is a verified cause->effect fact. 'mechanism' is backed by established, globally-accepted soil/ecological science. 'magnitude' and 'region_context' are backed by an India-specific study so the number actually holds for Indian conditions, not just a global average. Multi-hop reasoning walks these by matching one entry's 'effect' to the next entry's 'cause' — exact string match only, no fuzzy jumps.

connections.mechanism: Soil organic carbon is the primary energy and carbon source for soil microbial communities; raising it increases microbial biomass and activity.
connections.magnitude: SOC density raised to ~9.1 Mg/ha under agroforestry vs. degraded monoculture fallow baseline
connections.region_context: Semi-arid India, ICAR-IARI New Delhi field trial, 650mm mean annual rainfall
connections.mechanism_source: General soil microbial ecology (established, e.g. FAO soil carbon literature)
connections.regional_source: Rathore, S.S. et al. (2022). 'Integrated agroforestry systems improve soil carbon storage, water productivity, and economic returns in the marginal land of the semi-arid region.' Saudi Journal of Biological Sciences, 29(10):103427.

connections.mechanism: Healthier microbial activity supports more diverse flowering plant growth (via improved nutrient cycling), which sustains pollinator forage and habitat.
connections.magnitude: Qualitative link; not independently quantified for India in this dataset
connections.region_context: General mechanism, applicable to Indian agroecosystems
connections.regional_source: Chaudhary, O.P. & Chand, R. (2017). 'Economic benefits of animal pollination to Indian agriculture.' Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 87(9), 1117-1138. (ICAR) — establishes pollinator dependency baseline for Indian cropping systems.

connections.mechanism: Pollinators are a keystone functional group; their presence directly supports plant reproduction and downstream species richness.
connections.magnitude: 51.2% of 211 major Indian crops depend on animal pollination; pollinator-dependent crops account for 32.74% of India's total agricultural value (Rs. 4,22,827.52 crore)
connections.regional_source: Chaudhary, O.P. & Chand, R. (2017). Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 87(9), 1117-1138 (ICAR).

connections.mechanism: Animal pollination directly increases fruit/seed set in dependent crops; its loss causes measurable yield decline.
connections.magnitude: Oilseeds: 34.07% of yield value from pollination; Vegetables: 11.10%; Fruits: 14.82%; Cotton/fibers: 23.39%
connections.regional_source: Chaudhary, O.P. & Chand, R. (2017). Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences, 87(9), 1117-1138 (ICAR).

connections.mechanism: Converting mixed/natural land cover to monoculture removes structural and species diversity, fragmenting remaining natural habitat patches.
connections.magnitude: Core forest declined 14-26% (1989-2015) as non-forest land use expanded 14-29% across studied sites
connections.region_context: Northern Western Ghats, India (Anjaneri, Panchgani, Kas Plateau)
connections.regional_source: Badhe, Y.P. et al. (2024). 'Spatio-Temporal Changes in Forest Cover and Forest Fragmentation in the Northern Western Ghats.' International Journal of Ecology and Environmental Sciences, 50(1): 147-155.

connections.mechanism: Fragmented habitat patches support smaller, more isolated populations, increasing local extinction risk and edge-driven invasive species pressure.
connections.magnitude: Fragmented sites show increased invasive species incidence and human-wildlife conflict at forest edges
connections.regional_source: Badhe, Y.P. et al. (2024). International Journal of Ecology and Environmental Sciences, 50(1): 147-155.

connections.mechanism: Species richness is a core, direct component of overall biodiversity indices.
connections.regional_source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023.

connections.mechanism: Conversion of forest land to agriculture, plantation monoculture or built-up use directly reduces natural forest cover and associated carbon stock.
connections.magnitude: India's total forest + tree cover: 827,357 sq km (25.17% of geographic area); shift towards plantations flagged as a threat to natural ecosystems
connections.regional_source: Forest Survey of India, India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023 (Govt. of India, PIB release).

connections.mechanism: Wetlands and reliable water sources are critical breeding, feeding and refuge habitat; their loss directly reduces species survival rates.
connections.magnitude: India lost approximately one-third of its natural wetlands between 1940-2014; Chennai alone lost ~85% of its wetlands to urbanization
connections.regional_source: Status of wetlands in India research synthesis; reported via Mongabay-India (2024), citing wetland loss studies 1940-2014.

connections.mechanism: Population survival rates directly determine whether species persist in an ecosystem, the foundational unit of biodiversity.
connections.regional_source: Status of wetlands in India research synthesis; Mongabay-India (2024).

connections.mechanism: Tree/shrub integration improves soil structure and water retention, raising effective water-use efficiency per unit of applied water.
connections.magnitude: Water use efficiency up to 19.10 kg/ha-mm; irrigation water use efficiency up to 88.33 kg/ha-mm under integrated systems vs. fallow-monoculture baseline
connections.region_context: Semi-arid India, ICAR-IARI New Delhi field trial
connections.regional_source: Rathore, S.S. et al. (2022). Saudi Journal of Biological Sciences, 29(10):103427.

connections.mechanism: Diversified tree-crop systems add marketable produce streams beyond the base crop, raising net farm income per hectare.
connections.magnitude: Net returns up to 96.7% higher than fallow-monoculture baseline (US$3,529.1/ha vs. US$633.5/ha); benefit-cost ratio up to 3.85:1
connections.region_context: Semi-arid India, ICAR-IARI New Delhi field trial (2015-2018)
connections.regional_source: Rathore, S.S. et al. (2022). Saudi Journal of Biological Sciences, 29(10):103427.
